items.section: M5 Native State, Preferences, And Recents Foundation
items.title: Native state, preferences, and recents foundation
items.summary: Extract Wails runtime seams, add durable preferences, implement recents/workspace index, and raise non-e2e Go coverage to at least 80%.

items.title: Editable source token layer
items.summary: Replace the raw/split highlighting overlay limitation with an editable markdown token/decoration layer and implement marker hiding.

items.title: Responsive shell adaptation
items.summary: Define and implement graceful reduced-window behavior for the ribbon, side panels, contextual controls, mode controls, and status bar, including icon-only collapsed controls with accessible tooltips.

items.title: Cursor-precise document block model
items.summary: Introduce stable block targeting so contextual controls operate on the selected table, code block, diagram, image, or text block.

items.title: Image asset management
items.summary: Native and drag/drop image import, portable asset-copy policy, data-URI rendering with a visible missing-asset state, image-local width/alt/replace/reveal/delete controls, and print/export image support.

items.title: Comments and review workflow
items.summary: Add comment anchoring, persistence, review panel behavior, and resolved-state workflow.

items.title: Direct export pipeline
items.summary: Add direct PDF and HTML export artifacts from the formatted rendering pipeline while keeping Print as the OS print dialog path.

items.section: M11 Share, Sync/Git, And Extensions Architecture
items.title: Share, Sync/Git, and Extensions architecture
items.summary: Design and then implement separately backed Share, Sync/Git, and Extensions subsystems with explicit trust boundaries.

items.section: M12 Packaging, Signing, Updates, And Platform Hardening
items.title: Packaging, signing, updates, and platform hardening
items.summary: Add Developer ID signing, notarization, checksums, update-channel policy, packaged smoke tests, and later Windows/Linux packaging evaluation.

items.title: Give fidelity preservation a single owner
items.summary: Extract frontend/dist/src/fidelity/: one module per preservation implementing capture(original)/restore(serialized, state), with a registry owning the ordering. editor.js returns to owning only the Crepe lifecycle. Adding a preservation becomes one file plus one registry line rather than a three-place edit. Behaviour-preserving: the byte-identical corpus and the 49-construct survey must stay green and unchanged.

items.title: Move pure markdown logic out of the DOM adapter
items.summary: Command transforms, table operations, fence operations, image token parsing and link safety move from app.js (2835 lines, 189 top-level functions, ~10 domains) into pure string-to-string domain modules. Converts the bulk of the product's logic from browser-only verification to direct verification, without a Node toolchain. Must land as a sequence of small green extractions.

items.title: Separate Go use cases from the Wails binding surface
items.summary: Lift open, save, resolve-unsaved and asset import out of app.go (747 lines) into use-case types, leaving App as a thin adapter. The injected ports already exist and do not change. Sequenced last deliberately: dependency inversion is already in place, so this addresses comprehension rather than correctness, and deferring it costs clarity not safety.

items.title: Draw the host boundary before choosing a replacement
items.summary: Phase 0 of getting off Wails, approved 2026-08-10. One hostPort defined from what the application needs rather than what Wails offers, composing the existing nativePort rather than re-cutting 11 tested operations. tools/genbridge reads app.go via go/ast and emits a tracked bridge module, ending calls by name string and deleting three regex-based drift tests that generation makes impossible; the parser choice is a correctness requirement, since one of those tests matched 17 of 18 methods because UpdateContent is written on one line. Changes no runtime behaviour and ships an identical app, so every pre-existing test must stay green and unchanged. Its deliverable is a measurement: the host-specific surface reduced to main.go and transport.js and counted, so the choice between Wails v3, owning the host, and a macOS-native shell is made from evidence rather than estimate. Does not fix #61 or #57 and does not touch packaging, because all three need a host that exposes more than Wails v2 does.

items.title: An exit path from Wails
items.summary: Replace Wails with a hand-written host. Measured 2026-08-10: a working macOS host is 486 lines including its own test harness, against 241 for the boundary it replaces and 5,116 for Wails' macOS layer, with a panicking bound call REJECTING rather than hanging (#61). Raised to critical by a maintainer release gate: no further release ships until every vestige of Wails is eliminated. Two facts govern sequencing. The host is ONE CUTOVER, not a migration — bridge.js degrades when the host is absent but throws when it is partial, so no host can implement a subset. And packaging is the unmeasured item on the critical path: tools/build-macos.sh delegates bundle assembly, Info.plist templating, icon embedding and DMG creation to `wails build`, none of which the spike covered. Version identity must move off wails.json, with its drift gate, before that file is deleted. Full inventory: docs/decisions/2026-08-10-host-replacement.md.

items.title: Offer to become the default .md application
items.summary: Offer once, on first launch, to make Dr. Markdown the default application for .md and .markdown. The bundle already declares CFBundleDocumentTypes and UTImportedTypeDeclarations, so the app appears under Open With today and simply never becomes the default; no code calls Launch Services. Asked at first launch rather than "during install" because there is no installer -- distribution is a DMG with a drag-to-/Applications symlink. Claims the UTI net.daringfireball.markdown, covering both extensions the bundle advertises, via LSSetDefaultRoleHandlerForContentType: the NSWorkspace equivalent is macOS 12+ and the deployment target is 11.0, so it would need a version gate plus this call as the fallback anyway. Three guards: already the default, already answered, and running from a mounted disk image -- the last because setting the handler to a bundle under /Volumes points every future double-click at a volume that will be unmounted. Decision recorded in docs/decisions/2026-08-25-default-markdown-handler.md, with one question left open for the implementer to answer by driving the built app: whether recent macOS shows its own consent dialog, which would make our prompt the second one.
